## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

- Normal comparison arm: a fresh Ubuntu 24.04.4 VM had only its APT indexes refreshed before the chain, without installing updates. C1 reported 190 upgradable packages and C2 reported 151 packages with a newer security version. After the committed apply, C2 was 0 and C1 reported 51 remaining general updates. Package-version snapshots show 157 changed or added packages; for example OpenSSL and libssl3t64 changed from `3.0.13-0ubuntu3.11` to `3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16`. The committed spec passed 8/8 rows, and the second apply reported `changed=0`.
- Native evidence: Ubuntu unattended-upgrades `2.9.1+nmu4ubuntu1` help was captured and the real upgrade/dpkg logs retained locally. A subsequent direct `unattended-upgrade --debug` with `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` returned native rc=0 with no security updates remaining. Each of the removed flags was separately rejected with rc=2 on Ubuntu. Debian 12 unattended-upgrades `2.9.1+nmu3` help and trusted-origin metadata were captured in a disposable container; its `oldstable-security` archive and `bookworm-security` codename are covered by the committed native-metadata fixture.
- Stage controls: eight live check-mode arms used pilot-rendered, mutually exclusive staging/prod inventories of the same disposable VM. Confirmed staging and confirmed prod (attestation age 24 hours) passed; missing confirmations, age 169, age -1, environment mismatch and invalid stage failed for their intended reasons on the actual VM. Package and managed-policy hashes were identical before and after all eight arms.
- Native fault arms: a temporary PATH wrapper returned rc=42. With an existing managed policy, the play failed and restored identical bytes, mode 0640, UID and GID. With no original managed policy, the play failed and removed the new file. Both runs actually reached the wrapper. Package hashes and the active unattended-upgrades service were unchanged. These prove policy recovery, not package rollback.
- Effective-policy fault arm: a later APT fragment added an unrestricted Origins-Pattern. The merged-policy check rejected it before the native upgrade wrapper was invoked, the play failed, and the previous managed policy was preserved. A separate non-security `unattended_origins` override was rejected by the native-origin subset gate before upgrade invocation. Package hashes and service state remained unchanged in both cases.
- Every accepted fault arm started from the same healthy post-chain snapshot and was rolled back afterwards. All four arms used `ansible_ssh_args=-o ControlMaster=no -o ControlPath=none -o ConnectTimeout=15` to avoid connection reuse across snapshot restores. The normal full chain used its default transport; production source was unchanged.
- Local artifacts include the full normal-chain transcript, before/after package lists, native upgrade/dpkg output, stage-arm results and fault-arm results. They were retained for independent inspection; raw output is disposable and is not published in this record.

A dedicated `i172-r2` cache profile and `192.168.172.0/24` disposable network isolated this run from the existing dev-lite cache, whose stored Harbor credential returned401. The dedicated utility prepare wrapper remapped only its own syslog bind and APT host/container port, and retained generated internal settings when the Harbor input hash was unchanged. Native Compose health, API seeding and the actual APT proxy HTTP200 were checked. The committed pilot/apply source was not overlaid.
